cut.note: the primal simplex as GLPK organises it: a common storage area holding the current basis, the primal values of the basic variables (beta), the reduced costs of the non-basic ones (d), a two-phase flag (feasibility first, then optimality), and a pluggable pricing block (textbook, projected steepest edge, Devex); column choice and row choice (the ratio test) are separate modules with several strategies each. An inventory cut: the mechanisms are located by data structure and module, not read

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_name: spxprim.c struct csa (40-120): phase 0/1/2; beta[] with beta_st (undefined / just computed / updated); d[] with d_st; SPXSE se (projected steepest edge and Devex); orig_c / orig_l / orig_u copies; SPXAT / SPXNT sparse row-wise forms of A and of the non-basic columns N
organs.mechanism: phase 1 searches a primal feasible basis by minimising infeasibility, phase 2 the optimum; the basic solution and the reduced costs are cached and marked as freshly computed or incrementally updated so the iteration recomputes them only when the status demands; the pricing block scores non-basic columns by a reference-framework steepest-edge weight (or Devex's approximation) rather than the textbook most-negative reduced cost; the constraint matrix is kept both as A and as the non-basic part N in sparse row form for the two directions of multiplication
organs.input: an LP in standard form with bounds
organs.output: an optimal basis or a status
organs.state: the csa: basis, beta, d, pricing weights
assumptions: recomputing beta and d from scratch every iteration is the cost; updating them and refreshing periodically is the standard trade (Chvatal); steepest-edge pricing reduces iterations enough to pay for its weights
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a free simplex competitive on medium problems; the organisation every commercial code shares
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: numerical drift in the updated beta/d is why the status flags and periodic refactorisation exist; degeneracy handling (perturbation) not read
organs.source_boundary: spxprim.c and the chuzc/chuzr modules; CANDIDATE because bodies were not read

rejected_cuts.candidate: the basis factorisation library (bflib: LU with Forrest-Tomlin / Schur-complement updates), the dual simplex (spydual.c, spychuzc/chuzr), the interior-point solver, branch-and-cut (intopt), preprocessing (npp), MathProg (mpl), the API, the bundled MiniSat and AMD/COLAMD orderings
rejected_cuts.note: the directive of 2026-09-18 s1: no deepening of large COARSE bodies without a downstream question; bflib's basis update is the item if one arrives

rejected_cuts.evidence: two simplex variants, an interior-point method and a MIP layer share nothing but the problem object

pressures.condition: an organism pivots among bases of a sparse LP; the score is pivots to optimality and correctness of the final basis under floating point
pressures.failure_condition: cycling or an exponential pivot count (bad pricing), or a wrong optimum from drifted values
pressures.observable_consequence: pivot count and final residual on netlib LPs for textbook vs PSE vs Devex pricing, with refresh on and off
pressures.vacuity_condition: a problem whose first basis is optimal
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: an interior-point method (which the body also has; the world compares them)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the optimal basis must verify it in one iteration; textbook pricing must show more pivots on the degenerate netlib instances; no-refresh must show residual growth: the world must show all three

unexplained: one CANDIDATE organ from data-structure comments; nothing read in depth
